title: MR imaging of human brain metabolism using deuterated glucose at 9.4 T
summary: The energy metabolism of tumour cells differs significantly from that of benign cells and can be imaged, for example, using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI, so-called "nuclear spin"). The aim of this study is to develop magnetic resonance methods to measure the metabolic products or metabolic rates of tumour metastases in the brain. In the first phase of the study, these techniques will be tested and validated in healthy volunteers. After drinking or infusing deuterated glucose (a special sugar solution in which some protons have been replaced by deuterium), specific metabolic products can be measured in vivo (i.e. in the living organism) and metabolic rates can be estimated. In this study we want to show the metabolism of deuterated glutamine/glutamate and lactate in the healthy brain and in brain tumours. The high magnetic field of the MR-tomograph with a field strength of 9 Tesla (usually 1-3 Tesla in clinical routine) is an important prerequisite for this, as the spatial resolution increases with the field strength. These studies are of a purely scientific nature and serve to evaluate these new measurement methods. They therefore have no direct benefit for the participants, but are of great importance for future clinical MRI-based tumour diagnostics.

interventions.name: Healthy volunteers on whom deuterium magnetic resonance imaging (DMI) is to be performed (examination procedure: drinking of 250 ml glucose solution, after 15 min DMI of the head with different MR sequences in 9T MRI, measurement duration max. 2 h)

Patients with stage IV melanoma (metastases in the brain) in whom deuterium magnetic resonance imaging (DMI) is performed (examination procedure: drinking of 250 ml glucose solution, after 15 min DMI of the head with different MR sequences in 9T MRI, measurement duration max. 1 h)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For healthy subjects (Arm 1):
• Consent

For patients (Arm 2):
• Consent
• Stage IV melanoma with known brain tumor/brain metastasis
• Brain tumor/brain metastasis > 1 cm
• Brain tumor/brain metastasis with known contrast enhancement
Exclusion criteria:
For healthy subjects (Arm 1):
• Contraindications to MRI examinations
• Pregnancy
• Unwillingness to be informed about incidental findings
• History of diabetes mellitus or insulin resistance
• Clinical evidence of electrolyte imbalance
• History of malabsorption, extensive bowel resection or acute gastroenteritis.

For patients (Arm 2):
• Contraindications to MRI examinations
• Pregnancy
• Severe dysarthria/aphasia
• Unwillingness to be informed about incidental findings
• History of diabetes mellitus or insulin resistance
• Clinical evidence of electrolyte imbalance
• History of malabsorption, extensive bowel resection or acute gastroenteritis.
